items.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects six equivalent characterizations of a finite central simple algebra, including two matrix algebra conditions after extending scalars to the algebraic closure and to a separable closure, and the description via a finite central skew field (statement lines 984-1002). The proof is a complete argument: the first equivalence is a consequence of the definitions; the implication to the matrix algebra conditions uses the existence of a separable splitting field together with its Galois closure (proof lines 1007-1011); the converse direction uses that a base change of a matrix algebra is central simple (proof lines 1012-1014); and the last equivalence is Wedderburn's theorem (proof lines 1015-1017). The non-formal content is the arrangement of the circle of implications. The claim is H2.
